items.title: Al Tinney interviewed by Monk Rowe, Buffalo, New York, October 14, 2002
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] And we always think of those days and wow, Charlie Parker and Benny Harris... [INTERVIEWEE] That’s right, that’s right.

ctx.x: And we always think of those days and wow, Charlie Parker and Benny Harris, and what a thing, it must have been an amazing thing for all those people. But at the time everybody was just learning, is that right?

That’s right, that’s right. It was like the school. You know I had the band. The Boston Club made me the musical director for the band. And he let me hire who I wanted, and that was another workshop scene. I was doing the writing there for a small combo and I didn’t quite accomplish what I wanted to writing there. Because there was another guy that was writing and his writing sounded so good, you know I couldn’t match that so I just gave up writing, until, and that was in the forties or something. And I just gave…
